excerpt: Auriko is an LLM gateway built by former quant traders that routes each request to the cheapest suitable provider, accounting for prompt caching, latency and reliability. Pricing, alternatives and launch comments.
content:
Auriko is an AI gateway: one OpenAI-compatible API that sends your requests to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, DeepSeek and many other providers. What sets it apart is how it picks the route. Its founders describe themselves as former quant traders, and Auriko treats inference providers like trading venues. For each request it builds a list of eligible providers, applies your hard limits (model, capabilities, budget, data policy), then scores the candidates on cost, latency, throughput and success rate. The cost model goes beyond list prices: it accounts for each provider's prompt-caching rules and your own usage pattern, and re-evaluates every request, including mid-session when a cache may have gone cold. If a provider errors or hits a rate limit before responding, Auriko falls back to the next-best route.

Auriko publishes its own benchmark claiming an average 30% cost reduction against direct providers and other routers; that is the company's own test. It also offers fallback routing, bring-your-own-keys, budget limits by workspace or API key, and an analytics dashboard. Its privacy policy says it is a zero-data-retention proxy that does not read, log or store prompts and responses, and does not train models on your data. The company is Auriko, Inc., a Delaware corporation. Auriko launched on Product Hunt on 9 July 2026 and finished #1 for the day with 387 points and 72 comments.

We have not tested Auriko ourselves. This page brings together its official site, its Product Hunt page and the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

fit: run AI agents or apps with large, repeated contexts where prompt-caching rules change the real cost
use open-weight models served by several providers and want the cheapest reliable one per request
want automatic failover and budget limits across providers behind one API
not_fit: need identical output every time from one fixed provider: commenters raised drift between providers serving the same model (Auriko says it lists models truthfully, including quantization, and lets you pin them)
use only one provider's models, where a router adds less
need features still in private beta: parts of the site are marked private beta

pricing.intro: Auriko charges a platform fee plus the model providers' prices with no markup. Prices are in US dollars.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: All models, no provider markup, bring-your-own-keys, cache-aware and fallback routing, routing strategies, 1K platform RPM, 10K BYOK RPM, 5M BYOK monthly cap

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: Deterministic routing, multiple API keys and seats, unlimited RPM and BYOK cap, email support; 14-day free trial, no card

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: SSO/SAML, custom SLA, dedicated support, invoice billing, custom routing policy

notes: API usage is paid with pre-paid credits in US dollars, according to the terms.
Model providers' own prices pass through with 0% markup on every plan.

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: LiteLLM
items.what: Open-source AI gateway and SDK for calling 100+ LLM APIs with cost tracking, load balancing and logging
items.difference: You host and configure it yourself. Auriko is a hosted service whose pitch is cost-aware routing that accounts for caching.

items.name: Eden AI
items.what: One API to route between AI models for chat, OCR, speech, translation and more
items.difference: Covers many AI task types beyond LLMs. Auriko focuses on LLM inference cost and routing.

items.name: Mistral AI
items.what: Model maker offering its own open and commercial models
items.difference: A model provider rather than a router; Auriko could route to models like these.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Respan and Merlin Unified API as alternatives.

quotes.author: Gal Dayan
quotes.text: prompt caching usually rewards staying on the same provider for a session
quotes.reply: Michael Yang: routing is re-evaluated on every request using the expected cost of the whole session, so cache state is taken into account.

quotes.author: Hazy
quotes.text: When the cheapest provider starts erroring or its latency spikes, does Auriko fail over inside the same request?
quotes.reply: Michael Yang: yes, for retryable failures before a usable response it falls back to the next eligible path.

quotes.author: Ridhwik Vinod
quotes.text: Saving 40% on inference means nothing if my customer-facing outputs get worse
quotes.reply: Michael Yang: you can pin the exact model, including quantization, and routing stays within those limits.

faq.a: An AI gateway with one OpenAI-compatible API that routes each LLM request to the provider it expects to be cheapest while meeting your quality, latency and policy limits. It launched on Product Hunt on 9 July 2026.
It models each provider's prices, prompt-caching rules and your usage pattern, and scores routes per request. Auriko's own benchmark reports an average 30% saving; that is the company's claim.
The Free plan costs nothing beyond model usage, which passes through at providers' prices with no markup. Pro is $89 a month with a 14-day free trial; Enterprise is custom.
Its privacy policy says it is a zero-data-retention proxy: prompts and responses are not read, logged or stored, and routing uses metadata only.

faq.q: Can I use my own API keys?
faq.a: Yes. Auriko supports bring-your-own-keys, its platform keys, or both.

faq.q: What happens if a provider fails?
faq.a: For retryable errors such as rate limits, Auriko falls back to the next-best eligible route, according to its founder.
